title: Distinct seating arrangements
prompt:
Return every distinct arrangement of a row of guests given by their team codes, where guests with the same code are interchangeable, sorted lexicographically.

- values has 0 to 8 integers between -10 and 10; values may repeat.
- Each arrangement is a list using every value exactly once, and no arrangement may appear twice.
- Lexicographic order compares arrangements element by element. For an empty input return [[]].
hints: Generating all n! orders and removing duplicates with a set works, but wastes time on repeats.
Sort the values and fill positions left to right, marking which indices are already used.
At each position skip index i when values[i] equals values[i - 1] and index i - 1 is unused. Equal values are then always placed in index order, so each arrangement is built once.

solution.explanation: Sorting groups equal values together, and the skip rule forces copies of the same value to be used in index order, so each distinct arrangement is generated exactly once. Trying values in ascending order at every position makes the depth-first output lexicographically sorted.

complexity.notes: P is the number of distinct arrangements, at most n!. Each of the n levels on the way to an answer scans all n indices; only prefixes of real answers are explored.

followUps: Given one arrangement, compute the next one in lexicographic order in place, without recursion.
